description: SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over interaction histories. Learned item and position embeddings feed attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting sequence representation scores candidate items by dot product. Attention selects relevant recent or distant interactions. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
motivation: The paper balances the simplicity of short-context Markov models with the longer-context capacity of recurrent models. For this task, SASRec provides a sequential baseline across four categories with different interaction densities. Despite the supplied title, standard SASRec does not directly solve unseen-item cold start because it learns item-ID embeddings.
implementation_notes: Start from sasrec_perdataset and retain all four category routes. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and the effective SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Train with causal and padding masks, shifted next-item targets, and sampled-negative binary cross-entropy. Select changes using the host's macro validation HR@10 only. Keep the predictor writer synchronized with architecture changes and preserve the required diagnostic interfaces. No experiments or performance measurements were performed for this summary.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged training split.
  Construct padded history sequences and shifted positive targets.
  Sample negative items using training information.
  Encode item embeddings plus positional embeddings with causal attention blocks.
  Score positive and negative items with shared item embeddings.
  Minimize binary cross-entropy over nonpadding positions.
  Save category weights and matching predictor configuration.
Compare trials using host-provided macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential attention-based sequential recommendation approach.
originality.negative: Relative to the required SASRec baseline, this proposal introduces no new mechanism. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Allowed titles and descriptions could support a future content-aware extension for sparse items.
future_potential.negative: That extension is a hypothesis, not a result established here; any benefit requires validation within the search budget.

code_difficulty.positive: The supplied baseline already implements the main architecture and dataset routing.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require matching serialization, inference, and diagnostic adaptations. Higher scores indicate greater difficulty.
